speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long your child has been limping and exactly where they are feeling the pain? Also, has there been any recent injury or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain in the left knee seem worse in the morning or after periods of rest, and does your child experience any stiffness? I also need to know if he has had any recent upper respiratory infections or if there is a family history of joint problems.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate to your hip or thigh, or does it feel strictly confined to the knee joint? Also, when you bend your left knee, do you feel a clicking or locking sensation, or does it just hurt?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the localized knee pain without fever or trauma, does the pain ever radiate to your hip or groin, and does it worsen when you internally rotate your left leg? I would also like to request a pelvic X-ray to check for underlying hip pathology. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The pelvic X-ray (specifically of the left hip) reveals flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head, which is consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. Musculoskeletal examination notes tenderness on palpation of the left hip and pain elicited with passive motion of the hip, while the knee examination shows full range of motion and negative special tests for instability or meniscal tear. Vital signs are within normal limits (Temperature: 36.8°C, Blood Pressure: 100/65 mmHg, Heart Rate: 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate: 18 breaths/min).

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of femoral head flattening and fragmentation, combined with the referred knee pain, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.
